label: SQL
headline: SQL Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for SQL — from basic SELECT queries to joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs, and DDL.

items.name: SELECT
items.definition: Retrieve specific columns from a table.

items.name: SELECT *
items.definition: Retrieve all columns from a table.

items.name: SELECT DISTINCT
items.definition: Return only unique values, removing duplicates.

items.name: AS (alias)
items.syntax: SELECT col AS alias FROM table
items.definition: Give a column or table a temporary display name.

items.name: LIMIT
items.definition: Return only the first n rows of results.

items.name: OFFSET
items.definition: Skip a number of rows before starting to return results — used for pagination.

items.name: ORDER BY
items.syntax: SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY col ASC
items.definition: Sort the result set by one or more columns. ASC (default) or DESC.

items.name: ORDER BY multiple
items.syntax: ORDER BY col1 ASC, col2 DESC
items.definition: Sort by a primary column, then a secondary column for ties.

items.name: WHERE
items.definition: Filter rows to only those matching a condition.

items.name: Comparison operators
items.syntax:
=   equal
!=  not equal
>   greater than
<   less than
>=  greater than or equal
<=  less than or equal
items.definition: Compare a column value against a literal or another column. Use these inside WHERE clauses.

items.name: AND / OR
items.definition: Combine multiple conditions. AND requires both; OR requires either.

items.name: NOT
items.definition: Negate a condition — return rows where the condition is false.

items.name: IN
items.definition: Match any value in a list — shorthand for multiple OR conditions.

items.name: NOT IN
items.definition: Exclude rows whose column value appears in the list.

items.name: BETWEEN
items.definition: Filter rows where a value falls within an inclusive range.

items.name: LIKE
items.definition: Pattern matching. % matches any string, _ matches exactly one character.

items.name: NOT LIKE
items.definition: Exclude rows whose column matches a pattern. Opposite of LIKE.

items.name: ILIKE
items.definition: Case-insensitive pattern matching (PostgreSQL / some dialects).

items.name: IS NULL
items.definition: Return rows where the column has no value (NULL).

items.name: IS NOT NULL
items.definition: Return rows where the column has a value.

items.name: EXISTS
items.syntax: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t2 WHERE t2.id = t1.id)
items.definition: Return rows where the subquery produces at least one result.

items.name: COUNT
items.definition: Count the number of rows. COUNT(col) ignores NULLs.

items.name: SUM
items.definition: Add up all numeric values in a column.

items.name: AVG
items.definition: Return the arithmetic mean of a numeric column.

items.name: MIN / MAX
items.definition: Return the smallest and largest value in a column.

items.name: GROUP BY
items.syntax: SELECT col, COUNT(*) FROM table GROUP BY col
items.definition: Group rows with the same value so aggregate functions are applied per group.

items.name: HAVING
items.definition: Filter groups after aggregation — like WHERE but for grouped results.

items.name: GROUP BY multiple
items.definition: Group by a combination of columns — each unique pair becomes its own group.

items.name: COUNT DISTINCT
items.definition: Count the number of unique non-null values in a column.

items.name: INNER JOIN
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM a
INNER JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id
items.definition: Return only rows that have a match in both tables.

items.name: LEFT JOIN
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM a
LEFT JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id
items.definition: Return all rows from the left table, with matched rows from the right. NULLs where no match.

items.name: RIGHT JOIN
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM a
RIGHT JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id
items.definition: Return all rows from the right table, with matched rows from the left. NULLs where no match.

items.name: FULL OUTER JOIN
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM a
FULL OUTER JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id
items.definition: Return all rows from both tables, with NULLs where there is no match on either side.

items.name: CROSS JOIN
items.syntax: SELECT * FROM a CROSS JOIN b
items.definition: Return every combination of rows from both tables (Cartesian product).

items.name: SELF JOIN
items.syntax:
SELECT a.name, b.name
FROM employees a
JOIN employees b ON a.manager_id = b.id
items.definition: Join a table to itself — useful for hierarchical or comparative queries.

items.name: Multiple joins
items.syntax:
FROM a
JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id
JOIN c ON b.id = c.b_id
items.definition: Chain joins across three or more tables in one query.

items.name: Subquery (WHERE)
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM orders
WHERE customer_id IN (
  SELECT id FROM customers WHERE city = 'NYC'
)
items.definition: Use the result of an inner query as a filter in the outer query.

items.name: Subquery (FROM)
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT col, COUNT(*) AS n FROM t GROUP BY col
) AS sub
WHERE n > 5
items.definition: Use a query result as a derived table — must be given an alias.

items.name: Correlated subquery
items.syntax:
SELECT * FROM orders o
WHERE amount > (
  SELECT AVG(amount) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = o.customer_id
)
items.definition: A subquery that references columns from the outer query — re-runs for each outer row.

items.name: Scalar subquery
items.syntax:
SELECT name, (SELECT MAX(score) FROM scores WHERE user_id = u.id) AS top
FROM users u
items.definition: A subquery in the SELECT list that returns a single value per row.

items.name: WITH (CTE)
items.syntax:
WITH cte AS (
  SELECT col, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM table
  GROUP BY col
)
SELECT * FROM cte WHERE n > 10
items.definition: Common Table Expression — a named temporary result set that can be referenced in the main query like a table.

items.name: Multiple CTEs
items.syntax:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT ...
),
b AS (
  SELECT ... FROM a
)
SELECT * FROM b
items.definition: Chain multiple CTEs — later ones can reference earlier ones.

items.name: Recursive CTE
items.syntax:
WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (
  SELECT id, parent_id FROM tree WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT t.id, t.parent_id FROM tree t JOIN cte ON t.parent_id = cte.id
)
SELECT * FROM cte
items.definition: Self-referencing CTE used to traverse hierarchical data like org charts or category trees.

items.name: ROW_NUMBER
items.definition: Assign a unique sequential number to each row in the result set.

items.name: RANK
items.definition: Rank rows — tied rows get the same rank, and the next rank is skipped.

items.name: DENSE_RANK
items.definition: Rank rows — tied rows get the same rank, but no ranks are skipped.

items.name: PARTITION BY
items.syntax: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC)
items.definition: Reset the window function for each group — like GROUP BY but without collapsing rows.

items.name: SUM (running total)
items.syntax: SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
items.definition: Calculate a cumulative sum — adds up all previous rows up to the current one.

items.name: LAG
items.definition: Access the value from the previous row in the result set.

items.name: LEAD
items.definition: Access the value from the next row in the result set.

items.name: FIRST_VALUE
items.syntax: FIRST_VALUE(col) OVER (PARTITION BY group ORDER BY date)
items.definition: Return the first value in the window frame for each partition.

items.name: LAST_VALUE
items.syntax: LAST_VALUE(col) OVER (PARTITION BY group ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
items.definition: Return the last value in the window frame. Requires explicit frame clause for correct results.

items.name: NTILE
items.definition: Divide rows into n equal buckets and assign a bucket number to each row.

items.name: UNION
items.syntax:
SELECT col FROM a
UNION
SELECT col FROM b
items.definition: Combine results of two queries, removing duplicate rows.

items.name: UNION ALL
items.syntax:
SELECT col FROM a
UNION ALL
SELECT col FROM b
items.definition: Combine results of two queries, keeping all rows including duplicates.

items.name: INTERSECT
items.syntax:
SELECT col FROM a
INTERSECT
SELECT col FROM b
items.definition: Return only rows that appear in both result sets.

items.name: EXCEPT
items.syntax:
SELECT col FROM a
EXCEPT
SELECT col FROM b
items.definition: Return rows from the first query that do not appear in the second.

items.name: INSERT
items.definition: Add a new row to a table.

items.name: INSERT multiple
items.definition: Insert multiple rows in a single statement.

items.name: INSERT SELECT
items.syntax:
INSERT INTO table (col1, col2)
SELECT col1, col2 FROM other_table
items.definition: Populate a table from the results of a query.

items.name: UPDATE
items.syntax:
UPDATE table SET col1 = 'new'
WHERE id = 1
items.definition: Modify existing rows that match a condition.

items.name: UPDATE multiple cols
items.syntax:
UPDATE table
SET col1 = 'a', col2 = 10
WHERE id = 1
items.definition: Update several columns at once in the same statement.

items.name: DELETE
items.definition: Remove rows matching a condition. Omit WHERE to delete all rows.

items.name: TRUNCATE
items.definition: Remove all rows from a table quickly — faster than DELETE, not logged per-row.

items.name: CREATE TABLE
items.syntax:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  age  INT
)
items.definition: Create a new table with defined columns and data types.

items.name: DROP TABLE
items.definition: Permanently delete a table and all its data.

items.name: DROP IF EXISTS
items.definition: Drop a table only if it exists — prevents an error if it doesn't.

items.name: ALTER — add column
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE table ADD COLUMN email VARCHAR(255)
items.definition: Add a new column to an existing table.

items.name: ALTER — drop column
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE table DROP COLUMN email
items.definition: Remove a column from an existing table.

items.name: ALTER — rename column
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE table RENAME COLUMN old TO new
items.definition: Rename a column without changing its data or type.

items.name: RENAME TABLE
items.syntax: ALTER TABLE old_name RENAME TO new_name
items.definition: Rename an existing table.

items.name: CREATE INDEX
items.definition: Create an index to speed up queries that filter or sort on a column.

items.name: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
items.syntax: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx ON table (col)
items.definition: Create an index that also enforces uniqueness on the column.

items.name: PRIMARY KEY
items.definition: Uniquely identifies each row. Implies NOT NULL and UNIQUE.

items.name: FOREIGN KEY
items.definition: Enforce referential integrity — col must match a value in the referenced table.

items.name: UNIQUE
items.definition: Ensure all values in a column are distinct.

items.name: NOT NULL
items.definition: Prevent NULL values from being inserted into a column.

items.name: DEFAULT
items.definition: Set a fallback value used when no value is supplied on insert.

items.name: CHECK
items.definition: Reject rows where the column value fails a condition.

items.name: CASE WHEN
items.syntax:
CASE
  WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A'
  WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B'
  ELSE 'C'
END
items.definition: Return different values based on conditions — like an if/else in SQL.

items.name: CASE (simple)
items.syntax:
CASE status
  WHEN 'active'   THEN 1
  WHEN 'inactive' THEN 0
  ELSE NULL
END
items.definition: Match a column against specific values and return a result for each match.

items.name: COALESCE
items.definition: Return the first non-NULL value from the list — great for fallback values.

items.name: NULLIF
items.definition: Return NULL if both arguments are equal, otherwise return the first argument. Useful to avoid division by zero.

items.name: IIF / IF
items.definition: Inline conditional (SQL Server / Access). Use CASE WHEN for broader compatibility.

items.name: UPPER / LOWER
items.definition: Convert a string to all uppercase or all lowercase.

items.name: LENGTH / LEN
items.definition: Return the number of characters in a string.

items.name: TRIM
items.definition: Remove leading and trailing whitespace from a string.

items.name: SUBSTRING
items.definition: Extract part of a string — start position and length.

items.name: CONCAT
items.definition: Join two or more strings together.

items.name: REPLACE
items.definition: Replace all occurrences of a substring within a string.

items.name: LIKE pattern
items.definition: % matches any sequence of characters; _ matches exactly one character.

items.name: POSITION / CHARINDEX
items.definition: Return the position of a substring within a string (1-based). Returns 0 if not found.

items.name: LEFT / RIGHT
items.definition: Return the first or last n characters of a string.

items.name: NOW / GETDATE
items.definition: Return the current date and time. NOW() is standard SQL / PostgreSQL; GETDATE() is SQL Server.

items.name: CURRENT_DATE
items.definition: Return today's date without the time component.

items.name: DATE_PART / EXTRACT
items.definition: Pull a specific part (year, month, day, hour) out of a date value.

items.name: DATE_TRUNC
items.definition: Truncate a date to the start of a period (month, week, year, etc.).

items.name: DATEDIFF
items.definition: Return the difference between two dates in the specified unit (SQL Server / MySQL).

items.name: DATE_ADD / INTERVAL
items.definition: Add a time interval to a date value.

items.name: CAST to date
items.definition: Convert a string or timestamp to a date type.

items.name: FORMAT date
items.definition: Format a date as a string in a specific pattern (PostgreSQL). Use FORMAT() in SQL Server.

items.name: ROUND
items.definition: Round a number to a specified number of decimal places.

items.name: FLOOR / CEILING
items.definition: Round down to the nearest integer or up to the nearest integer.

items.name: ABS
items.definition: Return the absolute (positive) value of a number.

items.name: MOD
items.definition: Return the remainder of a division.

items.name: POWER
items.definition: Raise a number to a specified power.

items.name: SQRT
items.definition: Return the square root of a number.

items.name: CAST numeric
items.definition: Convert a value to a specific numeric type, controlling precision and scale.

items.name: CREATE VIEW
items.syntax:
CREATE VIEW view_name AS
SELECT col1, col2 FROM table WHERE condition
items.definition: Save a query as a named virtual table that can be queried like a real table.

items.name: DROP VIEW
items.definition: Delete a view (does not affect the underlying data).

items.name: BEGIN
items.definition: Start a transaction — changes can be rolled back until committed.

items.name: COMMIT
items.definition: Permanently save all changes made in the current transaction.

items.name: ROLLBACK
items.definition: Undo all changes made since the transaction began.

items.name: SAVEPOINT
items.definition: Set a named checkpoint within a transaction to partially roll back to.
